Ah what to say that hasn't been said? This is yet another entry in the "super hard, FML, I hate my life, I hate this game, FU" controller throwing hard-as-nails platforming genre. It's immediately comparable to Super Meat Boy and to a much lesser extent, Braid. I say Braid simply b/c of the soundtrack which has a wistful and relaxing approach while you meet your death over and over again.
Gamewise its just a simple platformer with some puzzle elements as you go along. You go through levels avoiding various traps and you slowly gain new abilities. You cannot jump in the first few levels. You cannot crouch in the first fewer levels, but eventually you can do both along with other abilities that you gain as you progress.
This game is recommended for two sorts of players. If you are a platforming masochist (as I am) and enjoy torturing yourself while you master the levels, this game is up your alley. I also recommend the game for the very strong soundtrack which is where the comparison to Braid comes in. There's a lot of piano, violin, and live drums rather than a drum machine, which gives the music a more organic feel to it. Frankly, the music is what kept me going as I found myself raging more and more (one look at my achievements will tell you how easy it is to rack up the easy deaths) at this fun, but torturous, game. This also feels by design as a more erratic soundtrack would make it harder to want to go for "one more level".
It's already low priced and its been bundled a couple of times which should make it an easy purchase for an SMB or platforming fan. At the time of this review I've not even covered a fraction of the levels, and with timed runs through every level, replayability is very high. Level design is smart even in the early stages.
If I had to choose a negative trait, I'm not much of a fan of the screen tint changes as you die more and more in the same level. It makes it harder to see the smaller obstacles and while its pretty obvious this is by design, it annoyed me more than I liked it.
Get it. Torture yourself. Enjoy the music and the very strong color this game exudes. And watch out for hidden traps and later on, the nets that will surely cause even more pork chops being served in Mr. Bree's lovely forest beginnings.
Controller is highly recommended to enjoy this game to the fullest potential.

I've waited a long time to write this review, because for some reason I got it in my head that I wanted to play the entire game before I formed a complete opinion. But now that the game is finished, I realize this was totally unnecessary. The Dream Machine is a god damn masterpiece. And you can tell this from the very beginning. I fell in love after being gifted the first chapters, and went on to immediately buy the next 3, then eagerly waited the final chapter. I was lucky to have come across it towards the end, and only had to wait a year. Others have waited over 8 years for its completion. And the devs (all 2 of them) kept the fans updated through the whole thing.
It was well worth the wait.
This point n click is ♥♥♥♥ing gorgeous. The sets blow me away. Every new scene I entered I spent the first few minutes just guessing what everything was made of. I think about how much work it must've taken to put it all together, and its just so impressive. Every chapter gets prettier and prettier. And that final one is just astounding! Some scenes are sweet, and even more are creepy. And I was physically uncomfortable more than a couple times. It was fantastic. Stop motion animation, made with all kinds of stuff like clay, paint, broccoli, pubes. It's really cool. The game looks great.
And that was just the art! There's even content behind that pretty face! The story was beautiful, and twisted, and at times very sad. It dives deep into a dream world with dark realities and harsh truths. There is no voice acting, you have to read. This is a big plus to me, cuz sometimes bad voice acting can ruin a good story.. But the music and the ambience set a perfect tone, and sculpt ominously soothing voices to imagine as you read.
As far as gameplay, the interface is very comfortable. Walk speed, and text speeds all adjustable, so you can click through the dialogue at a casual pace. Some puzzles were a bit challenging, but nothing a little more exploring couldn't solve. Many times you can find multiple solutions to a problem, or discover clues that lead you nowhere. But never in an annoying way. I thought exploring was very rewarding. Even when it didn't actually matter. I am told this is called "having fun". I had a lot of fun playing this game.
I would highly recommend. Don't even wait for a sale, just get it. The devs deserve it. Its probably grossly underpriced anyways considering how much time has gone into it. A serious labor of love.
Thanks for reading, and THANK YOU DEVS for the awesome experience. Wonderful game!!

An Open Letter To The Developers:
I just wanted to say thank you.
Thank you for making a platformer with responsive controls, that challenges me and makes me think. Thank you for supporting Gravis Gamepads; most Indie developers these days think that just providing support for the XBOX 360 controller is good enough, so I appreciate that you thought of the rest of us. Thank you for making a game that runs beautifully on my three year-old Big Box computer. Thank you for a game that is multidimensional, and that features an extraordinary, bright, appropriate color palette...and thank you for knowing when to mute that palette for dramatic effect. Thank you for creating a game that has thoughtfulness and depth in storytelling, emotion, and gameplay; just by simply putting puzzle pieces that can't be reached until Mr. Bree acquires later skills adds replayability (not to mention wanting to beat my own times). Let's call this a "soft" no.
Mr. Bree+ is a difficult and surprisingly dark and bloody platformer. You start with nothing but the ability to move back and forth, but quickly learn how to jump. From there, you unlock other moves (a crouch, a wall jump, and a double jump) that will let you go back to earlier levels and collect items you couldn't get before to unlock bonus levels. The difficulty scales fairly well, and the controls are good enough that you have a decent handle on what you're doing most of the time (although wall jumping takes some getting used to).
HOWEVER, this game has some major problems. The most important one is that this game must have some sort of memory leak or something, because the framerate is terrible and only gets worse as you keep playing. I could still manage to beat levels, but good lord is it ugly, and I can definitely see it throwing some people off. The game also does this thing where after every 5 deaths or so, the look of the level changes. The problem is that after the first 5 deaths on a stage, it changes to this very dark black and red theme,
. It makes it much harder to see what's going on, as there are some platforms that are hard to distinguish even when the lighting is normal, and it also makes some traps like the trapping pits basically impossible to see. At that point, it's almost better to just kill yourself 5 more times just to change the lighting to something more tolerable.
It's kinda hard for me to give this game a thumbs down, because I did like the level layouts and the controls are pretty much fine. But man, it just does NOT run correctly, in addition to having levels be almost unplayable for a period of 5 lives and a few bugs that freeze the game. I would say wait until a patch, but it doesn't seem like the devs actually plan on doing that. If it ever goes on sale for less than a dollar, maybe you'll get some fun out of it? But really, it's just a mess.

The problem is that this game is fun for about an hour at the start, and about an hour at the end, but the 5 or 6 hours in between are incredibly tedious, repetitive, and pointless.  You will run in circles for hours covering identical areas to find clues that tell you nothing and fighting the same enemies over and over, until any sense of fear or curiosity is burned out of you by sheer over exposure.  Even accidentally skipping over some minor and insignificant clue will force you to go back and search for it, only to learn that it "reveals" some uninteresting fact you had already guessed hours ago.
The sidequests are what ruin this game.  Even the sidequests that have a plot and point to them, you'll either figure out what happened or stop caring long before you finish the breadcrumb trail.  And the game forces you to do every single time sink of a sidequest to progress to the main story, requiring a huge amount of backtracking and busywork in a game that was already painfully repetetive.
I would mark it as neutral, just for the visuals and sound, which are excellent, but that isn't an option.  I can't really reccomend it unless you enjoy very slow, meticulous, and repetetive games.

When you first enter Betrayer, you're struck by the awesome monochromatic art design, the atmosphere of foreboding, and  you get filled with a great sense of adventure.
It doesn't last long however, each area being much the same as the last, with the same enemies, same mechanics, same scenery. Things that were once fun to run around and collect become a chore. Enemy types are very few, and do not scale well with the ever-increasing power of your arsenal. Monsters that were scary once soon become little more than roadbumps (unless playing on the highest difficulty). There is some decent flavor text scattered about in the side-quests, except the final story quest requires you to backtrack over every single area and solve every single mystery before you can beat the game, which once again turns something that could have been an interesting side-quest into a tedious chore.
I recommend only buying on a steep sale, or not at all.

Betrayer is a game developed by Blackpowder Games and uses the Unreal Engine 3. You play a character who has washed up on the shores on a mysterious land, you meet a woman in a red hood, and over the course of the game you need to find out what happened and where the heck everyone is, the game, as far as I heard is inspired by a true story
The game is a first person shooter type game with rogue-lite elements in it. If you die, you lose all your stuff and you have to go and find the stuff you lost, however you can turn off this mechanic in the settings menu. You have basic old weapons, such as a bow and arrows, a common pistol and a musket. All with their real reloading and such, and this gives the game a unique feel to it, but can be frustrating at times when hordes of enemies come after you
The game does introduce stealth into it however the stealth mechanics aren't the greatest and easily avoidable. The enemies in the game are terrifying, from the red eyed Spaniards roaming the land to the undead, all with their terrifying sound effects. The game as whole is scary and unsettling at times, but I wouldn't call this a flat out horror game
The game also introduces a mechanic where you can travel between the living world to the other world, an even more unsettling part of the game. In this section of the game you have to find graves, clues and souls whereas in the living world, you have to find locations, letters and evidence. Over the course of the game, you will meet the only living person besides you, which is the red hooded woman
The game as a whole is beautiful, although nothing eye popping, the game does manage to deliver in the environments and atmosphere, the game is mainly in black and white with red colouring pin pointing the Spainiards and the red hooded woman as well as clues and evidence. In the other world, the world is much darker. Thankfully, you do not have to play the whole 5 hours all in black and white and you can change the colour saturation to make the game more colourful, however, this cannot be changed in the other world
Now, to my main complaint. The overall length and repition. I have to say the story wise, the game is fantastic and really had me hooked in its 5 hour or so campaign, however, the constant running in the woods, shooting some enemies, finding letters and clues and graves and travelling to the other world and seeing some dialogue whilst shooting another set of enemies in a whole of 5 hours is boring and unnecessary. Honestly, the beginning of the game was really interesting, as well as the ending and nearing the final bit of the game, but the middle part of the game was so boring that I did not even want to finish the game
Betrayer tries to hook you in with its atmosphere and environments but fails on diversity in other stuff. The story was very interesting, but killed by constant chores in every single map that the game offered
Betrayer is one of those types of games that only a few people would enjoy, if you look games with a good story, fantastic atmosphere and environments, whilst running on your own with no help from the game but doesn't mind the long repition the give it a try, if one of the above doesn't strike your fancy, then I'd said, leave this game aside

This is a great little game and you can pass it off as educational. You play as Grimm (female version an option) and fight monsters through an ever expanding map. There are boss fights thrown in to keep things interesting. You "fight" by spelling out words from a selection of letters. It is a bit like scrabble. The longer the word the better. Words also have ranks, gold, bronze, silver. Letters like J, Q and Z being gold as they are often difficult to fit in words. Bosses and special enemies are given criteria for damage. For example "Use words starting with vowels.". There is also a "hangman" type of mini game in some levels.
The word grid has a variety of looks and tiles can be effected with poison, spikes, stone, etc. all having a multitude of effects and how they can be used or not used as the case may be. Power-ups, cosmetic items, potions all add to the games longevity and charm.
The main characters are well done, as are the monsters and bosses they fight. Each stage has 5 different goals, the first being complete the stage, second complete against the clock and so on. This makes the game a challenge and adds the replay or continuous play often missing from this kind of game.
The core mechanics are very well designed. The game recognises most words but not all (not sure what dictionary they are using). It definitely to have a good vocabulary and being able to spell is also a plus.
This is a thoroughly enjoyable game for all the family and I highly recommend it to all.

Incredibly short but well worth the $1.99 / 6 paid for the bundle price I paid.
I would recommend the game under normal circumstances because it is somewhat well built with destructive buildings, etc.. but there are a lot of issues that leave something to be desired...
The negatives are:
- The ai is terrible on all levels from Story, Easy +, etc.. ( They look at you through walls and start shooting holes through solid concrete walls to target you ); they need a slight modification so when someone comes into their field-of-view they have a slight delay ( hesitation based on target recognition to determine friend-foe ) before firing, or not..
- The "toggle" Objectives button isn't a toggle despite trying different keys ( such as caps lock, tab, etc.. )
- In addition to the objectives "toggle" switch not working, when you hold a button down to keep the results up ( also so you can see where your character is ) it turns itself off when entering / exiting vehicles among other circumstances.
- The player character is easy to lose; the camera system isn't intuitive.
- The camera system is absolutely is disgusting. It moves more to the top-right than bottom-left making it hard to aim ( while enemies can shoot at you when you can't see them meaning you end up needing to use the compass to line up the shots ) and it's easy for the crosshair to get lost in the effects ( because the crosshair is one color which doesn't negate on like-colors ).
- Driving is sluggish and non-responsive - also armored vehicles seem to blow up when side paneling is shot.
- Buildings don't seem to collapse after destroying all supports.
- Vehicle lighting can't be changed.. ie what the ai leaves you with is what you get.
- You can't drive 99% of vehicles; the doors have to be open to drive them ( ie cop cars, armored, etc but civilian cars are off limits )
If these would be fixed, it'd be an entertaining game.
Some positives:
- Everything is essentially destructable.. Buildings, trees, poles, etc..
- Decent weapon balance for a flat-plane shooter ( ie assume all shots are body / center-mass shots ) with some targets taking more shots to take down based on armor and range.
- Vehicle damage looks nice from what small bit I could see; it looked like the pole indented the hood as it should but these may be pre-fabbed and unimpressive ( stuck it in pros to give benefit of the doubt for the limited time viewing the game )
It's worth a look if you get it on sale. I was able to find it on Indie for $1.99 in a bundle of 6 or so games.

A worthy sequel.  Visually and mechanically a step up from the original Bioshock, though the story is a bit too convoluted for it's own good.  The combat is notably improved, and sticking splicers to a wall with a speargun is immensely satisfying.  The city of Rapture is more colorful and feels larger thanks to the giant windows and the walks on the bottom of the ocean.  It does feel a bit "gamey"; there are abundant set pieces and it's quite clear where one level ends and the next begins.  The addition of guarding a Little Sister as she harvests Adam from a dead body is novel at first, but wears thin after the third or fourth time.  Then you have to do it about a dozen more...  That's this game in a nutshell; if you liked the first game it's a safe bet you'll like this, but the "been there, done that" feeling does set in after a time.
The DLC (Minerva's Den) is not a bad crash course into Rapture either.  It crashed on a me a couple times and I had to disable DirectX 10 effects to get through it, so the noticeable visual downgrade didn't do it any favors.  Still enjoyable, however, even if it feels like a disconnected story set in the Bioshock universe.  The ion cannon and singularity plasmid are highlights.  My main complaint (besides the crashing) is the muddy objectives which lead to feeling like you're a rat in a maze at times.  If you can get it rather cheap and aren't burned out on the series it's certainly worth checking out.

This game seems to get a lot of hate from hardcore MTG people, but I find it to be fun but flawed.
Pros:
- Fun strategy/tactics of MTG on your computer!
- Free! It is truly possible to earn all the coins in game and get all the cards, though it will probably take you a while.
- You can build many decks from the cards you have collected. (No limit as far as I know)
Cons:
- I generally preferred playing against the AI in Magic 2014, but with Magic Duels every AI opponent feels the same.
- I also like playing Two-Headed Giant in Magic 2014, where you can have fun with a friend and earn a card for you deck with each victory. Unfortunately, you get no coins playing Two-Headed Giant in Magic Duels. This makes you feel like you have a choice: do what you like to do but waste time, or do what's not quite as much fun to make progress gathering cards.
- The method of accessing your created decks discourages experimentation. If you create 50 decks, you have to scroll through them. This makes it difficult to choose the one you want.
Ways to improve:
- Improve deck organization
- Add coin rewards for Two-Headed Giant
- Add more variety to the AI decks
Overall Impression:
I enjoy the game and continue to play it. They have made good changes, such as upping the coins for each quest. Hopefully they will continue to tweak it as they expand the cards that are available.

For those wondering, the majority of my listed playtime was spent idling for cards. I've actually beaten the original Flash incarnation of this game before, so this is less a review and more of a comparison/series of general thoughts.
Mr. Bree was, and still is, an enjoyable cartoon platformer. Through a series of 60 levels, you'll control the titular pig as he runs and jumps through a series of increasingly-difficult locations, ranging from simple forests to abattoirs and everything in-between.
I never got the sense that this was as difficult as any of the Meat Boy games, as there seemed to be a lot of leeway in difficulty - I never felt it was impossible to complete a stage, and the levels feel like they were designed to reward people who practiced the wall-jumping/double-jumping and wanted to speedrun them.
Much like Meat Boy, though, the story is near-irrelevant fluff meant to tie certain worlds together. The whole pretext of the story is a pig waking up with amnesia after escaping from a slaver, and he has forgotten most of his basic skills. I felt that this concept (of having to learn your abilities) could have been taken a lot further. While there are opportunities to go back to earlier levels and get items with unlocked abilities, the levels themselves never really play up the fact that you're limited in mobility for a certain stretch of time. Contrast that to something like Don't Move, which rewards you based on trying and/or failing to increase your mobility or set of abilities. Once you unlock double-jumping, most of the levels become a breeze and there's no real threat to any of the obstacles.
Still, I found it to be an enjoyable romp, and for the price point (usually around $3, but less during sales), you could do a whole lot worse.

Fantastic visuals, great story, and buggy gameplay concisely sum up The Dream Machine.  An enormous amount of work clearly went in to making this point and click adventure and it pays off thoroughly.  But be warned, save often.
First off, the art is great. It is all hand crafted stop-motion models which are beautifully detail and adds quite a bit of surealness to the experience.  While there are times the animation feels a little sparse, there is never a time were backgrounds feel half done. Every bit of this game has a lot of care put into its visuals.
The story is exceptional, well themed and conceived.  It compares our inanimate selves actively dreaming to the concepts of birth and death.  The story maintains well thought out themes of reverse aging, passiveness vs assertiveness, dreams and freedom. Further, the story goes to very dark places at times. It can be gory, creepy, sexual, blasphemous, incestuous, and even delves fully into abortion. Be aware the darker plotlines are unavoidable so if they are not to your taste, you should avoid this game.
The game play is point and click adventure and it does it very well. Interestingly, there are at times multiple solutions and even small side plots you could optionally visit.  For example at one point you need to fetch some food for a character, different kinds of food can be acquired from different sources and prepared in different ways, all are accepted.  That is a charming bit of extra work that you do not often see in point and click adventures.
But there are some down sides, the game pacing and linearity isn’t consistent.  The first chapter is insanely short, while the last few could take quite a while.  Moreover, some sections of the game play more like a visual novel where you just keep clicking through dialogue; a big part of chapter 6 is like this and it really pulls you out of the game.
But the biggest failing is the bugs, during my play through the game crashed 8 times with no warning.  The crashes weren’t even repeatable, just random.  Luckily, the auto save is decent enough, but if you hate replaying, save often.  The more disconcerting bug happened when an event was supposed to trigger that would have killed my character but didn’t.  I was left thinking I solved the puzzle, and aimlessly wandered about for quite some time before I realized something was wrong.
So despite the bugs, the game is fantastic. It is dark and creepy, but done in a way that is artful and well balanced with the story and themes. Give this one a try if you are not afraid of story that takes you to places you might not want to think about.

The worlds are full of traps, so you may die a lot trying to figure out how to get through the level and collect all items. The game was coded using Flash, so basicly it has no way to utalize the hardware of my PC which in turn makes it glitchy, constantly crashing, and after a few levels time seems to slow down so reaction times for me are still the same, but projectiles and traps engage so slowly that I can easily out manuver them and avoid them. At first I thought the slowing effect was part of the game because I was dying so much, but once I restarted the game, the effect was gone until I beat a few more levels and then it was back again.
Maybe it has something to do with the fact that I am running a 5 year old computer with an i5 2.3 ghz processor and a ATI HD 5470 graphics card with 512 mbs of ram, but I doubt it. Other platformers play perfectly with exception to Fez which is understandable considering it's complexity. I want to like Mr. Bree+ but as it stands broken right now, I highly recommend that you save your $3 and put a down payment on a less buggy platformer.

Back in 2006, a game was released by Capcom, makers of one of my favorite series as covered here, Resident Evil. The game saw a lone photo-journalist, Frank West, fighting for his life against a relentless horde of zombies which had taken over the town of Willamette, New Jersey, mostly its mall. The game was lauded for its excellent graphics and atmosphere, Frank’s ability to pick up basically any item in the game-world and wield it as a weapon, as well as the game’s ability to keep track of dozens, even hundreds of zombies at once, but was criticized for its lack of a decent save system and slow, even deliberate controls.
While I did enjoy Dead Rising and its sequel (this time starring Chuck Greene, contestant on a reality game show that exploits zombies for entertainment) for its good points, it was those two major criticisms which I must report occur in both games, which turned me off to them in the end.
Sure, you get to see dozens of zombies all shambling towards you, wanting to eat your brains; that’s what they do, right? Unfortunately, even though you’re an ex-motocross champion (in the sequel), you have just about as much difficulty getting around as Frank West did – and more often than not get chewed on by the ravenous undead while you’re just trying to get from point A to B.
I would really, really enjoy this game, I have no doubt, if it were more forgiving; the graphics are indeed wonderful and evoke a feeling of being alone in an excellent-looking mall with hundred of the poor infected souls. I do enjoy seeing what kinds of weapons I can find in my environment (to the point of absurdity; hoisting a park bench and carrying it around as easily as an electric guitar?!), and the story this time around is more compelling; Chuck has to find extremely scarce medicine for his daughter, who was bitten by the zombies.
But again I have to say thumbs down to this game for its annoying checkpoint/saving system. To be more specific: there are now multiple save slots, which is quite good indeed, but there are still no checkpoint saves! If you let yourself get hurt one too many times while you’re far away from a bathroom – too bad, you just lost around twenty minutes of slogging through the zombie apocalypse. I would have liked at least a checkpoint for each new event or location in the mall that you enter, for anything can happen even in these little shops.
If you are patient, if you can concentrate on multiple things at the same time, if you are prepared to be punished, sure, I’d recommend Dead Rising 2. It’s a great game; it’s just not for me. I’ll be generous for its great graphics, sound and atmosphere and give it three out of five stars.

I hope it won't come as a surprise to anyone that I was an English major, and I work as an editor now. I've learned a lot about the power and uses of words over the years spent in books and text files, and that necessitated learning a lot of words, too. So I'm in a unique position to appreciate Letter Quest, the game I've been inadvertently preparing myself for my whole life. And I do appreciate it quite a bit for its polished presentation and its wealth of content, but mainly for the surprising challenge it offers.
The quest part of Letter Quest centers on Grimm, a plucky little reaper with his heart set on some pizza. A bevy of fanciful monsters is set against him reaching his goal, however, and so there's reaping to be done if a pie is in his future. That reaping is done by spelling words, of course, picking tiles from sets of 15 to form the longest words you can think of. Longer words do more damage and earn you more rewards, both of which are key for progressing though the game.
There's way more strategy here than just spelling SAT words, though. You'll mainly want to shoot for longer words because you're trading blows with enemies and need to clear the stage before they whittle you down. But sometimes it's better to save a long word for the next foe and finish off the current one with little terms. Enemies also have skills that can affect your letters, like poisons that do damage if you use that tile, whirlwinds that change letters every turn, and diseases that spread and make letters do no damage. It's not all bad, though, because sometimes crystal tiles appear that provide boons if you use them, so the better play can often be making a shorter word that uses the crystal to gain its effects.
These are just the tactical considerations during battle, mind you. Clearing stages and defeating monsters earn you gems that can be spent on equipment, potions, and an impressive spread of other items. You have books that provide focused bonuses when equipped, upgrades to your key stats and random effects like crystals appearing, unlockable weapons with different behaviors, and so on. There are consumables and cosmetic effects offered as well, so racking up gems isn't a purely functional endeavor either.
Spending your gems wisely is important to progress through the levels because the difficulty curve isn't a straight shot. Just doing the basic levels in order will get you outclassed within an hour or two, with enemies easily outdamaging you. You can be a spelling savant but because you're always trading blows with enemies, the true key to survival is having your stats in the right place. This might sound like a pain and honestly it can be a bit frustrating to be right on the edge of where your stats can get you, losing levels by just one or two turns.
The saving grace, though, is that each level has multiple challenge modes to attempt and score extra gems. Half of these are time attacks that tax your brain with spelling complex words on the clock, and the others are special gimmicks like limited words or 4-letter-only challenges to keep things fresh. Add to that some side paths through the world map into harder levels and you'll have plenty to keep you busy across the game's 40 stages. Oh, and there's even an endless mode if you tire of questing for letters and just want to spell some monsters to death.
It's a polished package, with nice clean vector art and a charming soundtrack to accompany your word assaults. Between the menus and the gem-based progression gating it does still resemble its mobile roots, however, so it's bound to feel cheaper than other offerings. For a game like this it's hardly the kiss of death, given how much depth and challenge there is to the gameplay. Letter Quest does a lot to build on the basic word-based combat, more than enough to keep anyone spelling their way through its dungeons.

I must say, I have
about this game:
On one side it is a really new and admirable approach to War Games. Especially since I grew up in Lebanon in the mid 90's, I can relate to some of struggles although never being in such extreme situations myself. It really gives you sometimes choices that are not really choices but moral dilemmas... and the absences of heroes and any kind of fantasy-element here, makes you feel every decision more than in many games I've played. The Lack of "Save" and "Load" Button, makes it naturally more realistic, you can just die because of some coincidence, or being in the wrong place at the wrong time and that’s it. There is no going back, to correct your mistake or use a different approach. You just died, cause this is how it happens in wars. It's always random and final.
On the other hand, I must admit the game play is a bit dull and repetitive. You can almost never complete all the objectives, go to all places or get all the upgrades... But this is not the purpose of this game. Whenever you finish a campaign a new one appears, there are 12 all together with different constellation of characters and different weather conditions and etc. But there are only 2 variations for housing, and also for the most places you go to scavenge. So after 3-4 runs, you already know where the bandits are, what tools to take, when to run and when to fight, which makes the replay value pretty low. I did all the campaign though, the game was too personal to me to leave it before that... 129 hours of dilemmas, small joys and bitter failures. I think if the creators did a bit more diversified environment, would have gone long way.

It comes across as a standard First person shooter in a lot of respects, namely melee feels weak sauce and you're only real weapons are ranged. At time of writing I haven't actually finished the game but I still recommend it but that's more for the story and the different take on things.

Not wishing to give too much away despite this game being a few months old now I'll leave you to discover that one.
All in all I'd recommend this game on the basis of that the company is trying something new and what they've created is both beautiful in design and implementation.

After carefully reading the reviews I decided to give the Bioshock Ultimate Collection a chance. The Collection comes with both the original and remastered editions, so even if you experience problems you will be fine.
So far I have not had a single crash in my playthrough. The game looks great and plays great.

If I had to sum this game up, it would be that the devs tried making a game that people would want to play, rather then making a game people would want to keep playing.
This game has a unique look with a monochrome art style that uses red to show points of interest, and if that's not your thing you can switch to full colour or anything inbetween. The game also does very little hand holding as it gives you a few tips of how the game works at the beggining but after that the game expects you to explore and work out everything else by yourself which isnt exactly a bad thing as I enjoyed the game more for it simply letting me work out things on my own.
The combat however is just awful, I liked the idea of using a bow to silently take out enemies and how you can use the wind to mask the noise you make but I found this was just a waste of time as enemies can spot you quite easily if your not crouching and the render distance for the red colouring that makes the enemies stand out is rather low. Enemies can only be silently killed so long as you hit them in the head with a bow or melee them, but if the arrow doesnt kill them every enemy for a few hundred miles round will know exacly where you are.
The gameplay itself isnt all that bad as you explore the area looking for clues and chests but after the first hour or so you will quickly grow bored of it as you will find that you've experienced everything this game has to offer after about 20 minutes. Run to the marker on your map, collect treasue, kill enemies nearby rinse and repeat. The story is also lackluster with an ending that just left me wondering why the devs even bothered adding it in.
Even after all these faults though I found myself enjoying the experience the whole way through even when I knew I was just repeating the same mundane steps the whole way through. If you give the game a chance I'm sure you will enjoy it even though it has many glaring issues.

Roller Coaster Tycoon 2 is a fun addictive sim game, where the goal is to create a park and achieve a specific objective. Whether it be get so many people to your park, have a high park rating by year 3, etc. You can achieve this by creating rides, adding decorations, hiring staff members to keep the park in shape, adding food stands, the list goes on and on.
While Roller Coaster Tycoon 1 was the original, this game feels like it takes it one step further. Cleaning up the UI, adding new decorations, fixing some AI and adding completely new rides. Now you may be thinking, "why by this version when I can buy RCT3 which is in 3d?" Thats where I think they went wrong by making the game 3d. It doesnt have the charm that this game has.
I did have a problem where the game was crashing on me whenever I saved or loaded game. I managed to fix it by running the game in Windows XP (SP2) and admin. I'm running Win. 8.1, so this fix might not work for all of you.
All in all I recommend this game to people who like casual games, sim games, fun games (not really a category but the game is fun), heck even a hardcore gamer might like this (Im a hardcore gamer so hopefully you share this opinion) For a great value of $10 you can have hours, upon hours of entertainment, which includes everything RCT2 has to offer! I had the basic version of the game when I was a kid, so to see the new stuff they added that I never got to experience makes the game even more worth it.
Overall I give this game a 8.5/10. Get this game, its completely worth it!

Despite being a game about a spree killer, it feels like the devs actually
controversial elements as much as possible - there are no kids (even the old 2D Fallout games let you kill kids!), no religious elements (i.e. asking victims if they believe in God), no political agenda, no targeting of specific groups, no torture, no nothing.
One of my most memorable gaming experiences was a level of Cannon Fodder where you had to blow up several bases that kept spawning enemies. The only way to blow them up was with a cannon in the middle of the level, but if you tried to use the cannon, the enemy's bazooka guys would blow you up. So first you had to go around the whole level and kill every bazooka guy. After all that trouble, it was very satisfying to hop into the cannon and easily blast every base. THAT is how a game about a spree killer should work - killing helpless victims isn't challenging, so it isn't fun by itself, so it needs to be the REWARD after you've accomplished the game's real challenges. I mean, how great would it have been to play as the Hatred guy BEFORE the rampage? Imagine you're buying nails and fertilizer at the hardware store, and the cashier makes some crack about how happy is that you're finally going to fix up your busted eyesore of a house, and he "can't wait to see the final product!" I mean, how much more satisfying would it be to blow up his store with a pipebomb then? SO much more!

Brutal platformers are basically small levels with tricky jumps and an emphasis on speed. Mr. Bree+ delivers 60 levels of gameplay, but with a far more forgiving difficulty curve than many of its competitors.
The concept is simple, you play as the titular character, running and jumping through 60 progressively more difficult levels. As you waltz through the early stages, you will collect various abilities to aid you such as wall jumping, double jumping, ducking and sprinting. Each level also has a bonus collectible item to find which is usually in a tough to reach spot. Collecting enough of these unlocks the more difficult stages later.
Mr. Bree+ is best described as a mashup between Super Meat Boy and Toki Tori. There is less of a focus on speed and momentum, allowing you to take your time and work out the best way to deal with a particular problem. It also has frequent checkpoints so you don’t have to replay the level from the start if you should die. This makes completing the game considerably easier than Super Meat Boy, by borrowing the reduced difficulty, slower pace and level design from Toki Tori. The levels themselves usually involve avoiding spikes, either on the floor, walls or flying through the air. Levels also contain camouflaged traps such as pits or nets that fall from the ceiling, as well plenty of moving platforms.
Aside from the core stages, the game packs a plethora of achievements which involve collecting items, completing stages within a time limit and without dying, as well as a few pointless ones such as watching the end credits all the way through. In general, they do add an extra challenge if you found the main game too easy.
The game doesn’t control nearly as smoothly as games like the aforementioned Super Meat Boy, or others like They Bleed Pixels. This is likely down to the slower pace, but most certainly a lack of polish on the way Mr. Bree handles. For example, since double jump and wall jump are the same button, he often doesn’t quite know which one to do. Add to this occasional game freezes, Windows 8 compatibility issues and odd bugs like starting a level lodged inside a wall, or a gate not triggered open properly if you press the switch in a certain way, you have a disappointing number of annoying bugs to deal with as well, albeit rarely. These should be relatively easy to fix, but no word as of writing on an update.
Mr. Bree+ has a plot, but the developers really tried too hard and got a little too ambitious (Slavery? Really?). The sorts of emotions they try to convey simply do not hit home for several reasons. For starters, the game is just too simplistic for any sort of serious storyline to be taken seriously. Secondly, a lot of the text appears at the bottom of the screen during the game, most of it is missed because you’re too busy concentrating on actually staying alive, the text also disappears so fast that you wouldn’t be able to read it anyway. Even if you did get the chance to read it, you will find many grammar and spelling errors and just bad English in general.
The visuals are a mixed bag, with some elements shining while others drag the experience down to the point where it affects the gameplay itself. For starters, the character animation, for a budget title, is simply wonderful. The character sprites are fully animated, along with impressive stylised artwork in the cutscenes. Level design assets are less impressive, with most of them being static and having little variation or consideration for making something aesthetically pleasing to look at. Lastly, the biggest flaw with the graphics by far is that the framerate is locked to 30FPS, which is an absolute travesty for this genre of game.
Audio also has its ups and downs. What few sound effects there are come through as mundane and generic, as well as having little variation despite being used repeatedly. On the other hand, the soundtrack is awesome, I mean REALLY awesome. The soundtrack alone is worth the asking price for this game, in my opinion. The soundtrack is not available through Steam, but can be found on Bandcamp for $1.
In summary, Mr. Bree+ is an inexpensive introduction to this particular platforming sub-genre. The budget price is justified by the various quality issues, but is fully competent at what it does and the effort that has been put into the presentation shines through in many aspects. A delicious pork chop, even if it does get stuck in your teeth on the way down.
Pros:
~Cheap
~Balanced and steady difficulty curve
~Good visual presentation for a budget game
~Great soundtrack
~Plenty of content, good replayability value
Cons:
~Several unnecessary and annoying bugs, glitches, freezes
~Framerate locked to 30FPS
~Disappointing boss fights
~Embarrassingly bad plot

If you really like games like TF2, or even something like Overwatch, then it's likely that you may enjoy Primal Carnage. This is a really good game for dinosaur fans, and just any other gamer alike. The human classes are all different, and somewhat unique, whilst using the original basis of a support class, damage dealer, etc. The dinosaur classes also bring a lot to the table, as you get to play as iconic dinosaurs that you've never reallyt had the chance to ACTUALLY PLAY AS! Despite this there are a few flaws. First off, this is the older version, and is definately not as good as the recent Primal Carnage: Extinction. Sometimes, when playing, I felt that the humans can be easily overpowered by dinosaur classes when in any gamemode. Also, if you're looking for scientifically accurate dinosaurs, this is not the game for you. If you want that, go support Saurian. So in the end, Primal Carnage is a good game. It's not a great game, but it has its pros for sure. Out of a 10 star ratio, I'll give this game a 7/10. Thanks for reading, and I hope this helps fellow dinosaur gamers!

If I had to sum this game up, it would be that the devs tried making a game that people would want to play, rather then making a game people would want to keep playing.
This game has a unique look with a monochrome art style that uses red to show points of interest, and if that's not your thing you can switch to full colour or anything inbetween. The game also does very little hand holding as it gives you a few tips of how the game works at the beggining but after that the game expects you to explore and work out everything else by yourself which isnt exactly a bad thing as I enjoyed the game more for it simply letting me work out things on my own.
The combat however is just awful, I liked the idea of using a bow to silently take out enemies and how you can use the wind to mask the noise you make but I found this was just a waste of time as enemies can spot you quite easily if your not crouching and the render distance for the red colouring that makes the enemies stand out is rather low. Enemies can only be silently killed so long as you hit them in the head with a bow or melee them, but if the arrow doesnt kill them every enemy for a few hundred miles round will know exacly where you are.
The gameplay itself isnt all that bad as you explore the area looking for clues and chests but after the first hour or so you will quickly grow bored of it as you will find that you've experienced everything this game has to offer after about 20 minutes. Run to the marker on your map, collect treasue, kill enemies nearby rinse and repeat. The story is also lackluster with an ending that just left me wondering why the devs even bothered adding it in.
Even after all these faults though I found myself enjoying the experience the whole way through even when I knew I was just repeating the same mundane steps the whole way through. If you give the game a chance I'm sure you will enjoy it even though it has many glaring issues.

about this game:
On one side it is a really new and admirable approach to War Games. Especially since I grew up in Lebanon in the mid 90's, I can relate to some of struggles although never being in such extreme situations myself. It really gives you sometimes choices that are not really choices but moral dilemmas... and the absences of heroes and any kind of fantasy-element here, makes you feel every decision more than in many games I've played. The Lack of "Save" and "Load" Button, makes it naturally more realistic, you can just die because of some coincidence, or being in the wrong place at the wrong time and that’s it. There is no going back, to correct your mistake or use a different approach. You just died, cause this is how it happens in wars. It's always random and final.
On the other hand, I must admit the game play is a bit dull and repetitive. You can almost never complete all the objectives, go to all places or get all the upgrades... But this is not the purpose of this game. Whenever you finish a campaign a new one appears, there are 12 all together with different constellation of characters and different weather conditions and etc. But there are only 2 variations for housing, and also for the most places you go to scavenge. So after 3-4 runs, you already know where the bandits are, what tools to take, when to run and when to fight, which makes the replay value pretty low. I did all the campaign though, the game was too personal to me to leave it before that... 129 hours of dilemmas, small joys and bitter failures. I think if the creators did a bit more diversified environment, would have gone long way.
Be unreasonable, and this game will be a hell of a ride !

I pre-ordered X-Rebirth and I think now it's the right time to give my opinion about this game. As a huge fan of X-series I have so much to say about this game, However I'll make this short because I'm just too busy and lazy to write a wall of text. The simple list will do (Public beta 4.10).
Pros:
- Stations are huge and they look cool (not inside thought). The several landing pads are making things little bit messy.
- Ships look very nice too and they are very detailed . You can actually destroy the different parts of the enemy ship like turret, engines, jump drives, shields etc..
- Capturing the ships is fun. I almost jumped in the air when I got my first K. Small fighter sized ships are useless though.
- Also the crew members are nice addition.
- Looking for hidden containers with long distance scanner is fun! There isn't unique stuff though...
- I like the reputation system.
- Engine boost and shields are using the same energy pool. It's nice addition because it makes more sense. For some reason the energy weapons doesn't need energy at all.
Cons:
- The Skunk is boring, ugly and and I hate my co-pilot. I really want to kick that redhead to the nearest nebula.
- Main character is also boring. Actually I don't see any reason why I would like to play pre-created character in this kind of game. So begone Ren Otani with your Skunk. I couldn't care a less about your pathetic life.
- Skunk has unlimited cargo space. Seriously!
- AI is absolutely terrible. Especially pathfinding. It collides a lot and controlling the drones is a nightmare.
- Capital ships that are following the player are very often stuck inside station structures and they can't move. Usually they are inside the station when you undock the Skunk.
- Fitting the ships (yes, even capital ships) is hard coded and there aren't any options to make custom configurations.
- Missiles are absolutely useless.
- Constructing the space station during the plot is waste of resources. The station doesn't have any kind of purpose.
- Game is crashing when trying to load quick savegame.
- DirectX 9.0c even the game engine is quite new. Not acceptable.
- Walking inside the stations is also boring. Most of the stations just looks the same.
- Character models are ugly and there are just few different models. Not even pony tails!
- Repetetive dialogues with NPC characters inside the stations is like some kind of punishment. You have to do that because that's the only way to train your crew but it's maybe the most annoying thing in whole game.
- Collecting containers (that are sometimes overlapped) inside space stations is just stupid.
- Egosoft has improved the GUI but it still sucks.
- All the capitals ships looks about the same inside. There is no any kind of command bridge. The crew is just standing around the launchpad.
- Inspecting station info -"points" around the stations doesn't make sense.

This review will contain (in this order): 1. My personal opinion 2. A description of one minor bug and how to avoid it 3. some hints about harder plot missions and how to finish them (without spoilers or cheating), as well as one or two general tips.
1. I first played this game in 2017 and completely missed any possible hype, or early problems, so my opinion is about the game as of 4.0. I actually had a lot of genuine fun and would place this game among the best games I played within the last year. This essentially plays like a better, faster, harder and a lot more beautiful Xbtf.
However, some people complained about the inability to fly any ships other then the start ship. The ability to change ships will return in x4, but just like Xbtf, Xrebirth is the story of one man and his ship getting involved in big events (somewhat Han Solo and Millenium Falcon like, you even sort of have your own (human) female Chewbacca). You can however still own other ships and stations and order them around.
Anyways. I enjoyed it a lot. The only thing that annoyed me, was that the NPCs were talking alot and I felt like they are generally unfriendly, but thats just me.
2. The "death by collison" no longer exists in this game, which causes the problem that you can glitch into big ships, if you approach them at high speeds from behind, while they are boosting. In the past, you would have most likely just exploded. Now you end up inside the ships structure. You can now try to glitch out, it sometimes works. Other than that, just reload. This happened to me about once every 10 hours of gameplay. Just carefully approach, aiming for the side, rather than the behind. If it happens, it wont hurt you, because you can now save anywhere and any time (unless dialogue is running). Other than that, I noticed some three times that the bodies of NPCs on stations had not yet loaded in (which made for funny moments, watching floating heads), but they alwways did after a few seconds. Last but not least, three ctds in over 100 hours of playing, which i link to some specific program running in the background.
3. The mission were you deliver some goods with your large tradeship. Trade now works a lot more realistic. Your trade ships now have to pull up next to the stations and then transports URVs will be send back and forth between the station and your ship. Just tell your ship to do the trade and wait. Like all thinks in all x games, it works somewhat faster and better of screen, so just leave the zone for a bit (dont need to leave the system), though you dont have to, because you can also watch the process if you want.
The mission were you are supposed to build a station in a specific system. Construction ships now need actual wares and builder urvs to build and the process takes some time (again, more realism). You will need bio-optic fibres and fusion reactors. Both are rare and wont be produced in the system, so you have to organize it yourself (transports assigned to a construction ship will only trade in the system the ship is in). Fusionreactors are especially rare. You can capture Sanahar transports with those wares, from the bad gouys, if you are somewhat lucky. Other than that, you can closely watch a specific facility in one of the albion zones (look up which one). OR just go to the home of light system, if you have the DLC and buy that stuff, HOL produces the things in abundance :D. Dont forget to do the smalltalk minigame with traders on those stations and ask them for trade updates, the stations trade offers can then permanently be viewed (need opnly once per station).
Last but not least,you can view your ships capture strength and enemy ships capture resistance in their respective general info parts. If yours is higher than the enemys, victory is almost assured.
Thats it, have fun.

It's not your classic X3 experience where you start in a fighter and end with a carrier with 50 of those docked in. But honestly, Egosoft devs knows what they are doing when it's about to make you feel in space. Recommended

One of my most memorable gaming experiences was a level of Cannon Fodder where you had to blow up several bases that kept spawning enemies. The only way to blow them up was with a cannon in the middle of the level, but if you tried to use the cannon, the enemy's bazooka guys would blow you up. So first you had to go around the whole level and kill every bazooka guy. After all that trouble, it was very satisfying to hop into the cannon and easily blast every base. THAT is how a game about a spree killer should work - killing helpless victims isn't challenging, so it isn't fun by itself, so it needs to be the REWARD after you've accomplished the game's real challenges. I mean, how great would it have been to play as the Hatred guy BEFORE the rampage? Imagine you're buying nails and fertilizer at the hardware store, and the cashier makes some crack about how happy is that you're finally going to fix up your busted eyesore of a house, and he "can't wait to see the final product!" Edited summary since I think people only looked at my score: With the workshop, this is one of the best space sims to date, I will gladly discuss any point of disagreement. Still not as deep as X3 but hands down better than Elite Dangerous. However, without it, it's clunky, confusing, dumbed down (yet still confusing) and near impossible to explore due to AI balancing issues....however it does looks better than ED either way.
This is a tough one to review. It's a good game. Don't let those ratings fool you. They are almost exclusively based around performance issues upon the game's release. Unfortunately yes it's taken this long to fix them all (that's how bad they were) and it does require a few easily added workshop mods to make it worth your time.The game is currently on version '4.0.' But, as such, 65 hours and I didn't experience a single c2d, minimal lag/screen tearing and all models and textures placed properly.
Legit.
Now, having said that, it ain't perfect. It does so, so many things right, even better than the other X games. However some bugs do still exist deep within, making the game playable but near impossible to finish; bugs like quests not triggering, wares not appearing, super strong enemies in low level areas...unfortunately what it does wrong it does so wrong it bottlenecks any greatness and instead of leaving you feeling like an epic veteran space captain, you feel like a helpless, injured lamb. Flying a spaceship.
Fortunately this is worst at the beginning of the game, before you've upgraded your ship and have a clue how to play. Things slowly improve over time. There is a steep learning curve (not as steep as the previous X titles but still steep) with very, very little explaining of information. The first 10 hours at least were just me trying to figure out how to navigate through the menus. Eventually you do feel at least semi-empowered and it is fun to just fly around and blow up enemies and capture ships.
Now, having said all THAT...the game 'can' be completed without any kind of mod...most likely, at least. But you will end up bald from stress and boredom about half way through. FORTUNATELY, and shockingly, this game has pretty active Workshop support...any game's saving grace. User made patches are godsends. There is also one called Simoom's cheat menu. Normally I would NEVER advocate cheating. I haven't actively cheated in a game since I was a little kid. I mean...what's the point? Well here the point is to be able to experience the game as it was 'meant' to be experienced, not as it currently is experienced. Making these ship modifications, making yourself not the ♥♥♥♥♥ of the universe...doing these things exponentially increases the games appeal and you get a feel for what the devs were trying to do all along.
And it's when you're at this stage, the game is easily an 8, arguanbly even a 9/10. The trade system, though a bit overwhelming, is quite expansive (once you've upgraded your trade software) and you do truly feel like an epic space trader, brokering deals between corporations and governments, swindling pirates, stealing ships and trading their goods, dozens of wares to choose from...it's incredibly versatile, albeit tough to figure out without Youtube and Google.
Combat, once your ship is upgraded, is also incredibly well done. Seriously, do not listen to these reviewers who likely didn't finish the game (or haven't updated the review in years. This is NOT the same X-Rebirth). The combat is some of the best space sim combat I've experienced. It's fast paced, intense, cool looking ships, multiple weapon and missile types...I mean it's awesome. The targeting system is easy to read and accurate. Dog fights are incredibly fun. The ship can be a little annoying since it doesn't always make it clear who's shooting at you from what direction, but once you get a feel for the game and learn the ropes this becomes a non-issue.
Graphics are good, but just short of mind-blowing. From a distance the game is nothing short of a-mazing. You can just sit there and admire the universe for hours. As you move closer, I don't want to say it get's 'bad', it just gets...generic. From a distance you imagine these intricate space ships and stations, then when you get to them and they all look the same and not particularly unique...I mean they're still cool and fun to use, it is a TON of fun and super exciting to weave in and out of space stations...but it does feel like it's missing what the French call a certain, "I don't know what."
Of course the worst part of the game would be the incessant need to land on stations. I say worst, but it's not like the 'worst' thing in the world, just get's repetitive after awhile. It would be the worst part of the game though. Fortunately your guy can run super fast and you can teleport back to your ship from anywhere...but you'll still wish you could just Comm in instead of having to dock and go walk around. It's fun for the first few hours, but it does get stale pretty quick. However compared to where it used to be, the stations are the most amazing thing ever and AAA status.
In conclusion, the game is an excellent space-sim. Probably one of the worst launches in game history, infinitely worse than Rome 2 or Arkham Knight, while simultaneously being one of the worst game's ever. BUT it is also one of the most phenomenal combacks ever. It's a good game guys, I promise. It's not NEARLY as space simm-y as X3, but it is still a fairly intricate space sim that gives you lots of control and will appeal to the casual space-captain far more than X3 ever could. Elite Dangerous isn't even worth comparing because they are so different. Literally the only similarities are space ships in space. So if you're deciding between the two, do you want a space trading/combat sim, or a space explorer?
I definitely recommend it on sale for $15-$20 or less, if not just to look at the graphics for awhile. If you like this sort of game, you will not be disappointed.

This is an extraordinarily playable spaceship-piloting game. Very simple and easy to get into, whilst yet providing enough customisability and choice to justify the "open world" tag, it drew me in from the first five minutes and kept me completely immersed until the endgame. It has an easy learning curve, but it doesn't sacrifice complexity overmuch.
Very pretty graphics and gratifying sound - the soundtrack, by the way, is PERFECT. And even if you don't like it, it has an amazing feature of being able to choose your own music, and assign it to different in-game scenarios. Reeeeeally nice touch.
The story is quite an interesting one for sci-fi fans, and there is a surprising amount of speech/animation for a game at this price point - enough to make it a genuinely fun campaign. There is even replay value in the amount of choice in factions and weaponry.
The only issue I have is that it's too short, in that the game initially hints at a large amount of content - ships; weapons; star systems, etc. and then simply makes these things very time-consuming to attain, and the end of the line- best ship; best weapons; final star system, happens a bit too soon, with the endgame lying on predictable lines from the progression set out on at the start.
To sum up - extreme value for money here - just don't forget you're not playing an AAA title, like I did, and be disappointed that it ends too soon.

Hatred is pretty much a modern remake of Postal (1997). It plays exactly like it. You run around and kill people for no reason.
Pros:
Aesthetic - The monochromatic black and white color palette is unique and looks amazing. It really makes things like explosions and blood stand out as they are one of the few things that have color in the game.
Destruction system - You can destroy pretty much everything in the level. Not only does it look awesome, but it makes firefights with cops and the army all the more exciting. Stuck in a house surrounded by SWAT? Chuck a grenade to a wall where a couple of them are concentrated. You'll kill them all and blow the wall up giving you an easy escape.
Neutral:
Combat and gunplay is your standard isometric shooter affair. It's nothing special but it is competent.
The executions are far too tame for my liking. The only gorey one is a curb stomp. Everything else is a stab to the head or a shot to the chest.
The free content patch that added Survivor Mode is decent. It's nothing special but free content is always something I support especially in this day and age where developers love to milk their games out with paid DLC.
Cons:
Bugs - Even after a bunch of patches the game is still full of bugs. It is still crash prone. There was also an entire level where the civilian AI bugged out and they all stood still as I shot them all up. None of them ran away or did anything.
Performance - Game runs like crap.
Controls - Keyboard controls are unresponsive. Hatred is unplayable with a gamepad because the pad controls are just abysmal.
Length - Hatred is only 3 hours long.
Worth picking up when it's on sale if you enjoy mindless shooters.

I guess we have all experienced it: starting a game we have bought in the spur of a moment during a summer sale, maybe along with a dozen others that turned out half-okay, half-not-so-okay, smugly thinking to ourself, "Well, let’s get this over with, shall we?" - only to find ourself blown away and feeling like a whole new person two nights later, albeit one that needs a shower and some fresh air. Like when you start watching Doctor Who because you have nothing else to do and end up building full-scale TARDISes for your cats, knocking four times every darn time before entering a room and telling your friends how much you’ve grown as a person watching it. But to be honest, no point and click adventure game has done this to me in quite the epic scale as The Dream Machine has. And having grown up with an older sibling with access to Leisure Suit Larry and Monkey Island, that is saying something.
So after half-heartedly convincing myself to try it, I almost startled a bit when I found myself laughing at the introduction to chapter 1. I mean an authentic laugh, not the face people make while typing “lol”. The game continued to surprise me with what unfolded to be an incredibly beautifully made little world full of amazing detail and a unique artistic style. And while it was cozy within its little walls, with its jazz and ambient music, I found it to be packed with possibilities for exploration.
So the playdoh-dollhouse really brought the childhood memories on their way. But what really gave me that sense of "this feels like the first time I've ever played a PC game" and “this is the way I actually see things when I don’t think about it too much”, was how well the shape and sound of the game were complemented with its storytelling and dialogues. The dialogues, because they showed a truthful yet non-judging and loving understanding of human nature. And the storytelling, because it managed to remain relaxing and innocent throughout the game while at the same time consistently mounting in suspense and surrealism. And in more than one instance one has to flatout admire the way it shows things in such a truthful manner that is rare in computer games: that people sometimes do things that seem dark and morbid, but then they are genuinely sorry and apologize; or that the elderly lady from next door with her teapots and doileys at some point of her life did have a sex life, such as it was.
The makers of The Dream Machine have taken all those little impressions of life that are usually limited to be experienced in the privacy of our heads, and shaped them into something that can be shared - not as a clever book on psychology, but as a wonderfully made game everyone can enjoy. To me, this is what makes The Dream Machine so amazing, and if it does turn out that the makers want to publish the game’s script as a clever book after all, I will totally buy it.

The graphics are very good for such a low price game, but still have occasional issues. Certain things encountered appear blocky and rectangular, when they in fact should flow smoothly. I'm running on the highest graphic setting with a Radeon R9 290 GPU.
Physics/Mechanics/Engine: 8/10... Actually, 9/10
The combat is my only complaint. One could be aimed right at the head of an enemy at relatively close range, and the projectile will act like you're aiming well above your target, or to the right/left. A point-blank headshot turns into a projectile sailing 3 feet above their head. Another downside, if one of your projectiles gets stuck higher up in a tree; don't bother jumping to try and grab it. You just end up looking like a cat chasing a laser pointer. That said, a cool feature is certain projectiles can ricochet off armor, and still be retrievable (if one can find them.) My favorite feature though, is the use of directional sounds/hearing. Very well implemented, instills a good sense of distance/direction unlike some other games.
Pricing: 11/10
I bought the game on sale, curious at it's low price tag lowered even further by the sale. Looking deeper and reading other reviews, I decided to give the game a try. I'm glad I did, I feel as though by getting this on sale I practically stole it at $1.50 (or what ever the price of the sale was). I'd definitely have been happy if I still paid full price.
Atmosphere: 10/10
Many "horror" games claim they're soooo scary. All those games have is jumpscares with no build up. This game is different! It holds a very creepy atmosphere, and nowhere feels safe. When I play, I'm constantly looking behind and listening to the various noises hostiles will make. To me, this is a true horror game, not just another jump-scare fest. Eyes also hold a strong sense of fear for me, so when one of the types of hostiles got so close to me I could see them, I got goosebumps. A game hasn't given me goosebumps like that in a long long time.
TL/DR: Buy the game. If you like a horror game that can hold it's atmosphere and has a good story, you will be pleased.

First off, I have a lot more hours than steam shows into this game. I play offline at work with no internet. I probably have closer to 100 hrs or more into this game.
Short version: The game is great. It's a lot of fun. You can easily and happily sink many hours into it and still have not experienced half of what this massive game has to offer. The possibilities are seemingly endless. With that said, this game does have its down falls(mentioned below), some pretty annoying. But nothing bad enough to earn this game the rating it currently has. It is well worth the base price. If it's on sale, you should jump on it.
Long Version:
As it has been stated this game had a very rough start. That is long over with. The game isn't broke. Its much much better now.
I'll start with the good...
To start, I own all of the X games, as I got them all in a bundle. I have not played any of the previous titles. I tried X3 but I found it to be incredibly incredibly frustrating to learn and a little ugly/dissappointing in graphics next to this one. So I put it down and came straight to X: Rebirth. With that said, I can't accurately compare it to any of the previous X titles. However I can say, the X games have a nasty reputation for being super hard to learn and not holding your hand along the way. X: Rebirth is a deep game, it is harder than the average game to learn to play. You will need to do your fair share of tutorial vids and googling along the way. But it is SO MUCH better than X3. I picked it up fairly quickly. It is not nearly as frustrating to learn as X3. That for me is a major plus.
What I really love about this game are the possibilities, depth, and the sandbox like atmosphere. You can follow the main story, you can turn it off and do a great many of things, from different odd jobs, you can specialize in things like transporting/trading a huge number of different goods, bounty hunting, smuggling, passenger transport, policing/patrolling, be an evil space pirate(scan, hijack, loot, hack, pillage, sabotage, and destroy every thing you come across), Build massive space stations and create a HUGE and extremely profitable empire, engage in gigantic space battles worthy of a Star Wars movie, grow a fleet of ships or have multiple fleets, upgrade and mod your ship and ships in your fleet, etc.. the list goes on. That is what makes this game such a great experience for me.
Now the game as great as it is, has some pretty major downfalls that are pretty ill recieved. First off, and possibly worst.. (You probably already know) You only get the one ship. That's a bummer. I had hopes of being able to buy and garage a huge inventory of different ships. Upgrade them, customize them, mod them, etc.. This game doesn't have that. You can buy a ton of ships.. but you will not be piloting them. You will be hiring captains and pilots to do that for you and then you will order them to do your bidding. It would have been so much cooler to be able to personally pilot a huge freighter and transport/smuggle goods all by yourself. Or deck out a wicked fast/agile little fighter ship to wreak havoc in battle. Or captain a huge battleship and command a fleet of fighters in battle. Maybe go on the hunt for special/legendary ships... But no you just get the one ship. Now you can customize the ship by changing the cockpit configuration. You can buy new weapons, upgrade them, upgrade the engines, shields, software, scanner, etc. And then you can find and buy mods to use on your weapons to improve and/or alter their performance. This is probably the biggest downfall of this game for me.
The next biggest thing is, stations.. They are EXTREMELY bland and feel very unfinished to me. Every station you step onto is identicle to the last one. There are a couple of different variations that very mildly change them up.. but for the most part they are pretty much identical. They also feel incredibly lifeless. There are few NPC's on most of them (anywhere between 4 to 15(maybe)). Those NPC's stand or sit in one place, they do not walk or move. They don't work on anything or operate anything. If you go into a bunk room, they will all just be sitting on their beds or leaning against a wall not talking.. or doing any moving aside from blinking and maybe looking around. As often as you have to go onto stations the devs should have put more care into them and done something to make the process a lot more interesting.
The next thing, the NPC's and the whole smalltalk thing.. This is annoying and kind of dumb in my opinion. You can engage in smalltalk with the NPC's and if you perform well you can get special little benefits from them like a personal or station discount, told where to find a good job applicant, etc. However the only way to engage in this smalltalk is to wait around in a populated area like a bunk room and wait for one of them to talk. Sometimes it happens quick.. Sometimes you'll wait 10 - 15 minutes and not hear a peep. The things they talk about are annoying as well.. as you have about 3 -4 (maybe more or less) different conversation topics. When responding to them you have to stop a little sliding bar at the right time to "peform" in the conversation well, their responses to you have nothing to do with the conversation, instead they compliment or insult you based on how good of a talker you are lol. If you do this a couple times good enough then you can get access to the discounts or you can continue if you give them a gift. Also this improves or hurts your reputation with whatever faction the NPC belongs to. You will find yourself doing this a lot trying to get station discounts,  trade offer updates, better vendor prices, or whatever else. There are mods that help with this like Trade Agents Forever.. but there is still no way to completely avoid or get around it. This whole little mechanic is something that should have been completely scrapped, replaced, or whatever. It gets super old, super repetitive, and just annoying.
This is almost a non issue now due to the mod Capital Ship Bridges... But when you dock on capital ships, they have no bridge. They are all identical for the most part and just have the docking area. The mod makes it to where they have a bridge and a couple other small areas you can check out. The only reason I mention this is because the devs should have at least done what the mod does. Not only that, they should have made a somewhat unique bridge to each type of capital ship. Not a huge deal.. but just something that would have have helped with immersion.
The last thing that somewhat bothers me.. Sometimes when in a battle with small ships the AI seems a little wonky when watching the other ships. This is not a big deal, doesn't affect game play, doesn't break the game, just something a little silly looking. But every once in a while its like a ship will just stop midspace and rotate itself around a different direction and continue on. Instead of more realistically keeping the ship in motion heading forward and either looping back or banking around. I know space flight is probably nothing like flight on earth.. but we probably all imagine the flight mechanics to look similar to(or more intense/agile than) flying a jet, banking around, loops, cork screws, etc.. Not just coming to stop, slowly turning a different direction, then going on lol. Again its not a big deal, its just kind of a mood killer sometimes.. you'll be feeling like Luke Skywalker zooming around in an X-Wing after a baddie in a Tie Fighter.. then that baddie.. just stops midspace for something that looks as awkward and slow as a 3 point turn for.
There are some other things I could probably mention that would make the game better. But these things are the biggest and would make what is now a great experience into an outstanding and amazing experience. Obviously(saying that), I still think highly of the game and do not feel these issues ruin the game or make it not worth the price.
